notes:
CRM notes / summary: 
- Account: Stratiform Cloudworks — an established digital-banking platform (payment rails + fraud detection). Evaluating Redwood Dedicated with VPC/private control plane.
- Primary ask: Reserved GPU pool planning across multiple regions/AZs with clearly defined throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for customer-facing chat and reranking workflows. High availability and regulatory data residency are musts.
- Workload profile: mix of chat (multi-turn, avg ctx 1.5k tokens), reranking for search (short queries, high qps), and periodic embedding batches for fraud models. Peak traffic is predictable daily spikes tied to batch settlement windows.
- Performance targets provided by customer: p50 < 60ms for short-chat completions, p95 < 300ms for online chat (typical seq len 512), p99 < 750ms under 95th percentile load. Reranking: sustained throughput goal 12k qps across the US region; embedding batch windows need capacity for 150 concurrent embedding jobs.
- Capacity planning constraints: prefer reserved H100-class equivalents for predictive throughput. Want multi-region pools (us-east-1 primary, us-west-2 warm standby, eu-west-1 for EU residency). Request 30% failover headroom per-region (i.e., plan reserved capacity that can absorb a full-AZ failure without immediate autoscale).
- Failover/DR targets: RTO goal 120s for routing cutover, RPO minimal (stateless inference). They asked about automatic routing policies + prefix cache priming for standby pools to avoid cold-start latencies.
- SLA negotiation notes: customer pushing for explicit p95 latency SLO at regional level with credits for rollback. Legal wants: uptime SLA >= 99.95% for dedicated pools, measured per-region, and a deterministic latency credit schedule (p95/P99). AE/SE flagged these as negotiable; Redwood legal to review.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high; they are willing to commit to 12–24 month reserved contracts if unit economics are clear. Looking to compare net ARR vs. self-hosting on cloud marketplace.
- POC plan: 2-week Dedicated pilot across us-east-1 with H100-equivalent pool sized for 12k qps reranking and 6k tokens/s generation sustained. Metrics to monitor: per-token cost, p50/p95/p99, KV cache hit rate, batch utilization, and failover simulation results. POC soak + chaos test (simulate AZ collapse) scheduled during pilot.
- Technical asks from SE: details on kernel/quantization choices for their model family (decoder-only + cross-attention for reranker), recommended batching config (dynamic batching target 8–12), KV cache pre-warming approach, and runway for model upgrades.
- Integration notes: need SSO/SAML, audit logs forwarded to their SIEM, KMS integration for key wrapping, and a 7-year audit retention plan for transaction trace (they have compliance teams pushing long retention).
- Quotes from stakeholders: "We need deterministic latency for customer conversations during peak settlement windows — can't have spikes." — Head of Platform.
- Next operational steps: Redwood to deliver a revised regional reservation workbook that includes: AZ-aware placement, explicit failover headroom calculations, SLA language options (latency credit table), and an estimated price cadence for 12/24 month commitments.
- Stubs/refs: sizing workbook (drive link), initial SLA draft (drive), two call recordings (fireflies ids), legal thread in Gmail (thread-CA+20260301XYZ).
- Known risks: internal budget cycle ends 2026-03-31; legal may push back on latency credit exposure; their onboarding window for production is tight (targeting Q3 2026).
